Target: /workspace/amadus — Laravel 13 GDS training simulator (white-box source at /workspace/amadus). Call get_threat_model("/workspace/amadus") first. Your focus: AUTHENTICATION, ROLES, IMPERSONATION, MASS ASSIGNMENT. One job: can a cadet become an instructor (or an unauth user become anyone)?

SCOPE (files): app/Http/Controllers/AuthController.php, InstructorController.php, DashboardController.php (switchRole + section), PasswordResetController.php, app/Http/Middleware/EnsureUserIsInstructor.php, app/Models/User.php, routes/web.php, bootstrap/app.php, relevant Blade views (resources/views) for session/role handling.

STATIC ANALYSIS — map every route to its middleware and answer:
1. `POST /dashboard/switch-role` sits OUTSIDE the instructor middleware group (routes/web.php). Read DashboardController::switchRole: what does it accept, can a cadet set role=instructor? Is there server-side verification of actual role vs session?
2. EnsureUserIsInstructor: how does it decide? Session key? DB column? Can the session key be influenced by switchRole or by any other writer?
3. Impersonation: InstructorController::impersonateStudent + exitImpersonation (route under `auth` only, not instructor — check). If a cadet hits /instructor/students/{id}/impersonate directly, what happens? Is exitImpersonation usable by a cadet to gain the instructor's identity (does it restore the original instructor id from a session key the attacker can set)? THIS IS THE KEY CHAIN TO CHECK: cadet sets session impersonation key → exitImpersonation restores attacker-chosen instructor id → instructor privileges.
4. Mass assignment: register(), storeStudent(), batchStoreStudents() — which request fields reach User::create/update? Can role/is_approved/instructor flags be set by a cadet or unauthenticated register? Check User::$fillable/$guarded.
5. Auth flows: login (identifier? username enumeration?), register approval flow, password reset (token generation/validation, trustProxies(at:'*') + password-reset link poisoning via Host/X-Forwarded-Host — check how reset URL is built).
6. Logout (POST only? CSRF?), session fixation, /api/auth/me behavior.

DYNAMIC VALIDATION — check shared notes (list_notes) for "Scan runtime — URL + credentials" from the Runtime Bootstrap agent; if not there yet, do static first and re-check every few minutes (it takes a while — install PHP etc.). When available: log in as cadet via curl (save cookies), attempt switch-role to instructor, attempt instructor routes, attempt the impersonation/exit chain, attempt mass-assignment on register/storeStudent. Capture proving HTTP exchanges — note their proxy request ids (traffic is auto-captured) for http_exchange_ids. NEVER use identifiable names/markers in payloads (no tool/agent names).

REPORTING: for each confirmed issue file create_vulnerability_report (you are the reporting agent) with code_locations fix_before/fix_after (verbatim) + fix_pr_body, per the white-box workflow — derive the fix at report time. Run counterevidence pass first. record_coverage for every surface assessed (clean ones too). agent_finish with findings summary + open items.

Target: /workspace/amadus — Laravel 13 GDS training simulator (source at /workspace/amadus). Call get_threat_model("/workspace/amadus") first. Your focus: OBJECT-LEVEL AUTHORIZATION (IDOR/BOLA) + business-logic boundaries. One job: can a cadet read or modify another cadet's (or the instructor's) objects?

SCOPE: app/Http/Controllers/DashboardController.php, InstructorController.php, TrainingController.php, TerminalController.php; app/Services/Amadeus/PnrService.php + QueueService.php (ownership filtering); app/Models/*.php (relations); routes/web.php. Map every route that touches an object id / username / record locator.

OBJECT MAP — for each model (User, Pnr, Scenario, Submission, LessonProgress, QueueItem, TerminalActivityLog) determine: who owns it, which endpoints read it, which endpoints write it, and what check (if any) enforces ownership. Then test:
1. PNR access: RT/<record locator> and any PNR retrieve path — is lookup by 6-char locator scoped to the requesting user? Cross-cadet PNR read? PNR modify (add names/segments to someone else's PNR)? Ignore/cancel?
2. Submissions: /dashboard/scenarios/{id}/submit and grading — can a cadet grade (POST /api/instructor/submissions/{id}/grade is instructor-gated, but check any other writer)? Read other users' submissions via scenario listing?
3. LessonProgress saveProgress/getProgress: user scoping?
4. Spectate: /api/instructor/spectate/{username} — instructor-gated; but what does it expose (other instructor's students? any user incl. instructors?), and is the DashboardController::section('spectate') view equally gated?
5. Scenario create/delete: can a cadet create/delete scenarios (createScenarioApi is under instructor, verify) or read another instructor's scenarios? deleteScenario ownership?
6. Queue broadcast / sandbox reset (instructor): do they affect OTHER instructors' or all students' data — cross-instructor boundaries within the role.
7. Terminal activity logs: who can read whose command history (privacy of other students)?
8. destroyStudent/{id}: can instructor A delete instructor B's students — cross-instructor object authz.
9. /dashboard/{section} dynamic section: what sections exist, is any section rendering other users' data without a check?

DYNAMIC: check list_notes for "Scan runtime — URL + credentials" (Runtime Bootstrap agent may still be working — do static first, recheck periodically). When runtime is up: with cadet A and cadet B sessions (curl with cookie jars), prove cross-access end-to-end (create PNR as A, retrieve/modify as B; submit as A, inspect as B; etc.). Capture proving HTTP exchanges and note proxy request ids for http_exchange_ids. NEVER use identifiable names/markers in payloads.

REPORTING: confirmed → create_vulnerability_report with code_locations fix_before/fix_after + fix_pr_body. Counterevidence pass first; honest confidence; severity per demonstrated impact (training data + student activity privacy context). record_coverage per surface incl. clean ones. agent_finish with findings + open items.

Target: /workspace/amadus — Laravel 13 GDS training simulator (source at /workspace/amadus). Call get_threat_model("/workspace/amadus") first. Your focus: THE INSTALLER / pre-provisioning attack surface. One job: can an unauthenticated attacker take over a deployment through /install?

SCOPE (files): app/Http/Controllers/InstallerController.php, app/Services/Installer/InstallerService.php, app/Http/Middleware/EnsureAppIsInstalled.php, app/Console/Commands/InstallAppCommand.php, RemoveInstallerCommand.php, routes/web.php (installer routes), database/migrations + seeders if relevant.

STATIC ANALYSIS:
1. Lock logic: isAlreadyProvisioned() — what signals "installed"? (env flag? users table exists? instructor exists? file marker?) Any TOCTOU between the check and install()? Is the lock re-checked on POST /install, /install/requirements, /install/test-db? What happens on a deployed instance where the lock file/flag was never set (e.g. CLI install path vs web path differences, APP_INSTALLED env missing)? EnsureAppIsInstalled middleware — does it block or redirect when NOT installed, and does it cover the installer routes themselves?
2. POST /install input handling: what is written to .env (values from request?) — can attacker-controlled values inject newlines/env vars into .env (e.g. APP_URL, DB_*, instructor email/password)? Quote/escape handling in the env writer? Could injected env vars flip APP_DEBUG, change cache/session drivers, or achieve code exec later?
3. POST /install/test-db: attacker supplies host/port/username/password/database_path (validated only as strings). Does the service actually connect to the attacker-chosen host:port (MySQL handshake) → SSRF / internal port scanning primitive? Error messages → information disclosure (version strings, distinguish refused/timeout/auth-failed)? database_path — arbitrary file read via sqlite open ("file exists" oracle) or path traversal write? Timing-based port scan?
4. Instructor provisioning: does install() create the instructor account from request input (email/password)? Password strength/log? Race between installs?
5. InstallAppCommand (CLI): does it drop different artifacts than the web installer (lock mismatch)?

DYNAMIC: check list_notes for "Scan runtime — URL + credentials"; if the runtime is up (it may not be yet — the bootstrap agent is installing PHP), test: GET /install on a "locked" instance (expect lock behavior), and simulate a fresh-uninstalled state ONLY IF you can do it on a separate copy — do NOT break the shared runtime DB. If no runtime, static-only is acceptable but record needs_follow_up coverage for what you could not execute.
RULES: never use identifiable names/markers in any request or payload.

REPORTING: confirmed issues → create_vulnerability_report with code_locations fix_before/fix_after + fix_pr_body (derive fix inline). Counterevidence pass first; honest confidence. record_coverage for each surface (installer lock, env writer, test-db, CLI installer). agent_finish with findings + open items.

Target: /workspace/amadus — Laravel 13 GDS training simulator (source at /workspace/amadus). Call get_threat_model("/workspace/amadus") first. Your focus: INJECTION — SQL via the Eloquent layer and OUTPUT INJECTION (XSS/template) across the cryptic parser and Blade views. SCOPE: app/Services/Amadeus/*.php (AmadeusParser.php 2568 lines is the core — read it in chunks), app/Http/Controllers/TerminalController.php + DashboardController.php, all resources/views/**/*.blade.php, public JS if any.

STATIC SWEEP:
1. SQL: rg for DB::, ->raw(, whereRaw, orderByRaw, selectRaw, DB::select/insert/update, string-concatenated query fragments, dynamic column/table names from request input (search/sort/filter params in instructor student lists, queue views). SQLite backend — check stacked queries/unions where raw is used. Also check the installer service for raw DDL with interpolated names.
2. Output injection: every `{!! !!}` in Blade (rg), Alpine x-html / x-init with dynamic values, @json into inline scripts, terminal output rendering (how does the emulator render command responses — if it renders PNR names/free-text SSRs back into HTML, is it escaped? check the Blade view for the terminal and any JS that innerHTML's server responses), command history rendering, scenario content rendering in dashboards.

Target: /workspace/amadus — Laravel 13 (PHP >=8.4) app, sqlite default DB. This is INFRASTRUCTURE work for the whole scan: stand the app up so other agents can do dynamic validation. Call get_threat_model("/workspace/amadus") for context.

STEPS:
1. Install PHP 8.4 CLI + required extensions (sudo available): `sudo apt-get install -y php8.4-cli php8.4-sqlite3 php8.4-mbstring php8.4-xml php8.4-curl php8.4-zip php8.4-bcmath php8.4-intl` (adjust names to what apt offers; php8.4-cli candidate 8.4.27 exists). Verify `php -v` >= 8.4 and `php -m` covers pdo/pdo_sqlite/mbstring/openssl/tokenizer/xml/ctype/json/curl/fileinfo/zip.
2. PRESERVE USER STATE: back up the existing .env to .env.scan-backup (only if .env.scan-backup doesn't already exist). Point the app at a COPY of the sqlite DB or a fresh one: set DB_CONNECTION=sqlite and DB_DATABASE=database/scan.sqlite (fresh file is fine — migrations will create it). Keep APP_KEY from existing .env (or generate if empty). APP_ENV=local, APP_DEBUG=true is acceptable for the scan runtime. Do NOT touch the user's original database file.
3. Vendor dir exists. If `php artisan --version` fails due to missing packages, run `composer install --no-interaction` (composer may need install: `curl -sS https://getcomposer.org/installer | php` then `php composer.phar install`). npm/node_modules exist already; only run `npm run build` if Blade views fail to find the Vite manifest.
4. Run migrations + seeders ONLY into the scan DB: `php artisan migrate --force` and seed what the installer seeds (check database/seeders). The app expects an instructor account — check README/InstallAppCommand for how the primary instructor is provisioned; if the web installer is required, either run `php artisan app:install` non-interactively (READ its code first — make sure it writes only to your scan DB and .env) or create users via tinker using factories.
5. Create test users for the scan and write them into a shared note (create_note, title "Scan runtime — URL + credentials"): instructor + at least 2 cadets, with usernames/passwords you generate (random, no identifiable markers referencing tools/agents). Serve with `php artisan serve --host=127.0.0.1 --port=8088` in a persistent session (exec_command with tty=true, note the session id in the same note). Verify with curl that / returns 200 and /login works, and that a test login (POST /login) succeeds.
6. If the app hard-requires the installer lock flow, document exactly how you provisioned (or why blocked) in the note.

RULES: do not attack the app; do not send attack payloads; never use identifiable names/markers in any request. Keep every change reversible (backup files listed in the note). agent_finish with: runtime URL, DB used, users created, any blockers.

Target: /workspace/amadus — Laravel 13 (PHP 8.4) Amadeus GDS training simulator. Call get_threat_model("/workspace/amadus") first; it is the shared baseline.

YOUR JOB (static breadth pass ONLY — do not attack, do not run the app):
1. Baseline coverage bundle per the source_aware_sast skill into /workspace/amadus/strix_runs/static/ (create it):
   - semgrep scan --config p/default --config p/php --config p/secrets --metrics=off --json
   - build sg-targets.txt from semgrep scope, run ast-grep structural pass
   - gitleaks detect + trufflehog filesystem (both, JSON)
   - trivy fs --scanners vuln,misconfig,secret on composer.lock + package-lock.json paths
2. Build a ROUTE → CONTROLLER → SINK inventory from routes/web.php: for every route, note middleware chain, controller@method, and the dangerous sinks reached (raw SQL/DB::*, eval/system/exec/proc, file ops, unserialize, Blade {!! !!}, x-html, Storage::, response()->file, header/redirect with user input). Write it as a shared note (create_note) titled "Route→Controller→Sink inventory" so later agents use it.
3. Dependency CVEs: triage trivy/gitleaks output for composer.lock and package-lock.json. For each verified known-CVE finding (verify CVE ID + affected range via web_search when unsure), file create_dependency_report with advisory_cvss from the advisory and honest reachability from your usage analysis. laravel/framework ^13.17 is the main one to check. Do NOT report CVEs in dev-only tooling as high; note ecosystem context.
4. Secrets: any real-looking credential in the repo (not example/factory data) — investigate and note; file a report only if it is a genuine secret with impact.

RULES: never use identifiable names/markers in any request or payload. Record coverage (record_coverage) for each surface you assess, including clean ones (outcome no_issue_found where nothing found). PHP is NOT installed in the sandbox — everything here is static; do not try to run the app (another agent handles runtime).
FINISH: agent_finish with a summary of inventory highlights, dependency reports filed, and any open items.

entries.risk_area: Vertical privilege escalation via role switching
entries.evidence: switchRole aborts 403 for all authenticated users (DashboardController.php:84-91); role is never taken from request. Unauthenticated users are redirected. No session role key exists — all checks read $user->role from DB.

entries.risk_area: Instructor middleware bypass
entries.evidence: Middleware checks $user->role !== 'instructor' from the authenticated (DB-backed) user model; not session-influenced. The only session key it relates to (impersonated_by_instructor) is never consulted by this middleware.

entries.surface: app/Services + app/Http/Controllers — Eloquent query building (parser, dashboards, instructor lists, installer)
entries.risk_area: SQL injection via Eloquent layer / raw query fragments
entries.evidence: rg across app/ found zero raw-expression builders (no whereRaw/orderByRaw/selectRaw/DB::select/unprepared). All queries are Eloquent with bound values; DecodeService LIKE uses addcslashes('%_') + parameter binding; installer CREATE DATABASE requires ^[a-zA-Z0-9_]+$ + backtick doubling, and only reachable pre-provisioning. Dynamic probes (DAC with quotes/UNION, RT/AHMED' OR '1'='1, RT/'||') returned literal 'NO MATCH FOUND'/seed data — no SQL errors, no boolean diff, PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES not disabled but no injection point exists to exploit.

entries.evidence: rg over all resources/views found zero {!! !!} and zero x-html/v-html. Every user-data path uses {{ }} (HTML-escaped) or x-text (textContent). @json($students/$pnrs/$logs) embeds PNR free text: Laravel's Js::from hex-escapes < > / & as \u003C \u003E \/ — verified dynamically: marker payloads (SSR text containing , AP , RM

entries.surface: AmadeusParser RT command family (app/Services/Amadeus/AmadeusParser.php:2143-2380) — PNR IDOR

Fix chains cover both the index branch (:2237-2240) and the locator/surname guest exemptions (:2354, :2289).

Reset link request returns a generic message for known/unknown identifiers (covered by test suite). Throttles: login 10/min, reset 6/min.

entries.risk_area: CSRF on logout / session invalidation / API auth surface
entries.evidence: POST /logout without CSRF token → 419 (VerifyCsrfToken active, no exceptions in bootstrap/app.php). Logout invalidates session + regenerates token (AuthController::logout). /api/auth/me returns {"user":null} unauthenticated, user object without sensitive fields when authed.

entries.risk_area: Host-header poisoning of password reset links
entries.evidence: Poisoned reset link (Host: evil.example) carries a valid token redeemable on the real host; end-to-end takeover reproduced and verified at DB hash level. Filed as vuln-0004 with verified inline fix (ResetPassword::createUrlUsing pinning to config('app.url')); tests pass.

entries.surface: POST /api/terminal/execute — RT locator + RT surname retrieval, guest identity
entries.risk_area: Unauthenticated PNR disclosure (guest-exempt ownership check)
entries.evidence: Working PoC: unauthenticated RT<locator> and RT/surname read full stored PNRs; guest QE writes foreign-office queue rows; exchanges 296/292. Fix filed in vuln-0005.

entries.surface: POST /api/terminal/execute — RT single-letter index and RT/LM list-line retrieval
entries.risk_area: Cross-cadet PNR disclosure (unscoped single-letter index + RT/LM line retrieve)
entries.evidence: Working PoC: cadet B RT/S listed cadet A's locators; RT2 returned full foreign PNR; direct RT<locator> control correctly blocked. Fix filed in vuln-0006.

entries.surface: AmadeusParser ET/TTP/IR persistence paths + submitScenarioApi PNR resolution
entries.risk_area: PNR modify/overwrite by non-owner (ET, TTP, IR, submission)
entries.evidence: Live-verified: ET overwrite throws UNAUTHORIZED TO OVERWRITE RECORD LOCATOR for foreign records (AmadeusParser.php:1897-1900); TTP foreign PNR blocked (:2388-2391); IR only reloads own/instructor records (:1943-1948); direct RT<locator> returns RT_UNAUTHORIZED for authenticated cadets (exchange 292); submitScenarioApi resolves only the caller's own stored PNR and 422s otherwise (exchange 200). No bypass found around these named controls.

entries.risk_area: Cross-instructor scenario deletion + submission cascade
entries.evidence: Live PoC: cross-office instructor DELETE /api/instructor/scenarios/{id} of another office's scenario returned 200 and cascade-deleted its submissions (exchanges 240/244/246; 0 rows after). Cadet DELETE correctly 403 (245). Fix filed in vuln-0007.

entries.risk_area: Cross-instructor object access (students CRUD, spectate, approve/reject, impersonate)
entries.evidence: Live controls: cross-office spectate → 404, cross-office destroyStudent → 404; same-office spectate → 200 (expected feature: last 100 terminal commands + active PNR locator). Named controls: User::where('office_id', $user->office_id) in InstructorController :257/:287/:316/:353 and DashboardController :380-382, applied on every path to the object. Minor residual: spectate looks up by username with office scope but no role filter, so an instructor could spectate another instructor in the same office (single-academy trust model — noted, not reported).

entries.risk_area: Cross-user lesson progress / submission reads and writes
entries.evidence: Static + live: TrainingController :32/:99-137 scopes all reads/writes to Auth::user()->username and re-verifies claimed objectives against the caller's own TerminalActivityLog records; submitScenarioApi upserts keyed on own username (ScenarioService :246-261) and 422s when recordLocator names a foreign PNR (exchange 200); getScenariosForStudent only joins the caller's own submissions. gradeSubmissionApi office-scoped (DashboardController :487-491); no non-instructor writer route exists (routes/web.php — grade only under instructor middleware).

entries.risk_area: Role-restricted section access / cross-user data in dashboard views
entries.evidence: Live: cadet GET /dashboard/gradebook → 302 to own dashboard; studentView queries all data by own username (DashboardController :102-163); getActivePnrApi instructor ?user= requires target in own office (:268-277) — verified cadet ?user= other-cadet returns own/empty, not the target's. InstructorView lists office-scoped students/submissions/Pnrs (:174-237).

entries.risk_area: Classroom-wide / cross-instructor destructive operations
entries.evidence: Live: cross-office sandbox reset cleared only the caller's office (XOFF22 counts; LON1A0980 PNRs untouched — verified by office-grouped row counts after reset); log deletion scoped through office usernames (QueueService :315-342); broadcast takes office from the authenticated user (DashboardController :521). Residual (by-design risk, not defect): an instructor's full-classroom reset also clears queue items other instructors of the same office created — same-office trust model.

entries.surface: Terminal queue commands QS/QT/QD/QE — client-supplied state.officeId
entries.risk_area: Queue read/write scoping (client-controlled state.officeId)
entries.evidence: Cross-office cadet read proven live: QD 7 with spoofed state.officeId=XOFF22 returned XOFF22's broadcast item (XY77TT/XOFF PAX) vs honest officeId showing only own office's items (exchanges 259/239); unauth guest write QE/XOFF22/9C0 created foreign-office rows (exchange 166, DB-verified). Covered in vuln-0005 remediation (client-supplied office identity is the root cause — parser trusts state.officeId over the session's user record).

entries.surface: TerminalActivityLog read paths (dashboard analytics, spectate, instructorView)
entries.risk_area: Terminal activity log privacy (who can read whose command history)
entries.evidence: TerminalActivityLog reads are keyed to usernames the viewer is entitled to: own logs for cadets (studentView :114), office-scoped students for instructors (instructorView :183, spectateStudentApi :387). No route exposes arbitrary usernames' logs.

entries.risk_area: Scenario creation/read authorization
entries.evidence: createScenarioApi under instructor middleware (verified: cadet create attempt → 401/403 in exchange 169); scenarios are readable by all roles by design (shared curriculum — students drill on them via getScenariosForStudent); delete covered separately (vuln-0007). No mass-assignment of created_by (set server-side :432).

entries.risk_area: Active-PNR inspection parameter (?user=) authorization
entries.evidence: getActivePnrApi ignores ?user= for students and returns own record (:268-279); instructor cross-office target → 404 via office scope (verified same pattern as spectate). Cadet B requesting ?user=ofletcher got own empty result, not A's data (exchange: getActivePnr control, HTTP 200 hasActivePnr:false).

entries.surface: AmadeusParser auxiliary retrieval commands (RT flight/ticket, LM/LP lists, LPO/LPS, RO claim)
entries.risk_area: PNR retrieval via alternate indexes (RT flight/ticket, LM/LP, LPO, RO)
entries.evidence: RT flight-branch returns hardcoded demo PNRs (no DB read); RT ticket-branch is static demo text; LM/LP multi-list and LPO/LPS office-search return hardcoded demo records only (AmadeusParser :2017-2112) — cannot leak real stored PNRs; RO claim branches return static text and never touch Pnr table.

entries.surface: Installer lock logic (InstallerService::isInstalled, acquireInstallLock, EnsureAppIsInstalled middleware)
entries.risk_area: Installer lock bypass / pre-provisioning unauthenticated takeover
entries.evidence: isAlreadyProvisioned() = storage/installed file OR (users table + instructor exists); flock(storage/installing.lock, LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) serializes concurrent installs and re-checks the lock inside performInstall; EnsureAppIsInstalled middleware heals a deleted lock file from DB state and blocks /install* (verified live: GET /install → 302, POST test-db → 403, POST /install → 403 after lock deletion with instructor present). createInstructor() refuses to touch existing username/email (anti-re-open ATO). InstallerTest 18/18 pass.

entries.risk_area: .env injection / newline injection of arbitrary env vars (APP_DEBUG flip, cache driver change)
entries.evidence: Dynamically tested the vendored phpdotenv parser (vendor/vlucas/phpdotenv): newlines inside quoted values are re-joined by the multiline processor, so "DB_PASSWORD=x\nAPP_DEBUG=true" stays one value and cannot inject new variables; formatEnvValue's addcslashes escapes quotes/backslashes/$; lone trailing backslash doesn't swallow following lines. Both append and preg_replace update paths tested. No APP_DEBUG/APP_KEY/SESSION_DRIVER flip, no code-exec path.

entries.risk_area: SSRF / internal port scan oracle + link-local guard bypass + worker-exhaustion DoS
entries.evidence: hex 0xa9fea9fe and octal 0177.0.0.1 and trailing-dot 169.254.169.254. bypass the link-local guard and PDO connects (proved via TCP listener at 169.254.169.254:3306 logging a real connection from the server); silent-open ports hang the worker indefinitely (PDO::ATTR_TIMEOUT does not bound the initial read), wedging the whole artisan-serve deployment; closed vs open ports are distinguishable (0.04s vs hang). Fix applied and verified. Report filed.

entries.surface: SQLite path handling (InstallerService::sanitizeSqlitePath + testDatabase sqlite branch)
entries.risk_area: arbitrary file write/read via database_path (path traversal)
entries.evidence: sanitizeSqlitePath strips to basename + forces .sqlite inside database/ — arbitrary file write/read ruled out. testDatabase sqlite path creates empty file and reports basename only; only distinguishes "directory not writable" vs success — negligible oracle. Verified dynamically earlier in full install flow (sqlite install succeeded, .env DB_DATABASE=database/database.sqlite).

entries.risk_area: CLI/web lock artifact mismatch (CLI install leaving web installer open)
entries.evidence: InstallAppCommand calls the same InstallerService::markInstalled (storage/installed lock) and createInstructor (refuses existing accounts), so CLI and web installs converge on the same lock signal; RemoveInstallerCommand only ever writes the lock file, never deletes it. InstallerTest tests 07/09/11 cover this. No lock mismatch exists.

entries.risk_area: Host-header poisoning of APP_URL default / installer wizard
entries.evidence: X-Forwarded-Host flows into request()->getSchemeAndHttpHost() (trustProxies '*') and is reflected as the default app_url in the installer wizard (verified live: app_url: 'https://probe.invalid.example' vs control 'http://127.0.0.1:8099'). Blade {{ }} entity-encodes quotes so JS-string breakout is blocked; backslash-only Host values self-DoS the response. It only prefills the visible field and the operator must complete the 6-step install, so it is a social-engineering/UX weakness, not a direct ATO. Not filed as a vulnerability; fix would be pinning app.url default instead of request-derived host.

entries.risk_area: Weak credential policy / plaintext logging during provisioning
entries.evidence: Validated against the vendored phpdotenv multiline parser and against a live attacker-run full-install: password min 6 confirmed + Hash::make used; credentials are written to .env DB_PASSWORD via the escaping writer (no injection); lock written after provisioning; flock prevents racing installs (test 12 covers 409); no logging of plaintext password observed in response or lock payload.

entries.surface: Instructor/training workflow surfaces (submissions, progress, queue broadcast, sandbox reset, spectate) — business logic
entries.risk_area: Business logic (workflow bypass, state manipulation, multi-step flows: submissions/grading, progress, queue broadcast, sandbox reset, spectate)
entries.evidence: Business-logic boundaries were assessed by the IDOR & Objectz lane (completed 16:57): saveProgress re-verifies objectives server-side against the caller's own terminal logs (no trust-the-client grading); submissions/grading flow instructor-gated with office scoping; queue broadcast and sandbox reset verified office-scoped except two same-trust-tier residuals noted but not reported — (1) spectate lookup has no role filter so same-office instructors can view each other's terminal history, (2) same-office sandbox reset clears queue items created by other same-office instructors. Both are role-consistent within a single-academy trust model; no cross-tier impact demonstrated. Root recording on the lane's behalf to close the ledger.

entries.surface: Installer responses (/install/requirements JSON, test-db error messages, lock-state behavior, CLI artifacts) — information disclosure
entries.risk_area: Information disclosure (error messages, debug endpoints, metadata leakage via installer responses)
entries.evidence: Information disclosure on the installer surface was assessed by the Installer lane (completed 17:20): /install/requirements returns generic environment booleans; test-db error responses are deliberately generic (no reachability-oracle detail, no version strings — confirmed live); requirements/test-db/install all re-check isAlreadyProvisioned() and 403/redirect when locked; CLI installer leaves no lock mismatch (lock self-heals from instructor-exists fallback, verified live). The Host-header prefill of the wizard's default app_url was checked for JS-string breakout and did not break out ({{ }} encoding) — covered by entry 54d25e. Timing-oracle disclosure is the informational component of vuln-0008. Root recording on the lane's behalf to close the ledger.

gaps.detail: Runtime Bootstrap ran (status: completed) without recording any coverage. Whatever it examined is absent from this record.
